subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu streaming card full-content updates cause severe latency regression on long replies

question: Should Feishu streaming cards add an explicit low-latency append/delta or fallback mode, or should OpenClaw keep full-content CardKit updates only and pursue another cadence/queue fix?
rationale: Current main preserves the full-content behavior that fixed truncation, but a fresh live repro says the linked cadence-only PR did not fix the severe long-reply tail, so automation cannot choose the permanent Feishu API tradeoff safely.

options.title: Define Opt-In Low-Latency Mode
options.body: Keep full-content as the default, but allow an explicit append/delta or fallback mode only with live proof that final content remains complete in affected Feishu tenants.

options.title: Continue Full-Content Coalescing Only
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/91943 as the intended direction, but require updated live proof because the July 6 repro says it did not improve the multi-minute tail.

options.title: Defer To Upstream Limitation
options.body: If maintainers decide Feishu CardKit full-content latency is an upstream constraint that OpenClaw should not work around, close with streaming:false or raw-message delivery as the supported alternative.

recommendation.title: Define Opt-In Low-Latency Mode
recommendation.body: Keep full-content as the default, but allow an explicit append/delta or fallback mode only with live proof that final content remains complete in affected Feishu tenants.

likelyOwner.reason: The package metadata identifies m1heng as the Feishu plugin community owner, and this decision is specific to Feishu channel behavior.
